summary: Market sentiment has turned decisively bearish, with the Nasdaq sliding into correction territory, Wall Street's post-election rally fully erased, and the VIX fear gauge surging its most since April amid a retail trader sell-off that rivals the intensity of the Covid collapse. On the macro front, the Bank of England's first rate hike since 2023 — paired with warnings of further tightening — has rattled global rate expectations, while a potential U.S. debt-ceiling standoff following the election outcome adds fiscal uncertainty to an already stressed environment. At the sector level, energy is in focus as oil heads toward pandemic-era lows despite ConocoPhillips beating estimates and boosting its dividend, while opportunistic investors are selectively buying beaten-down bank stocks on the sell-off. The primary risk factors crowding traders' minds include escalating Middle East tensions — with Iranian-linked tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran's nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar, and Iran-Russia security coordination all threatening supply disruptions — alongside geopolitical instability in Israel and a wave of European flight bomb threats amplifying safe-haven demand. In the short term, markets face a difficult path given the confluence of tightening monetary policy, unresolved geopolitical flashpoints, deteriorating technical signals, and political uncertainty in Washington, with any relief rally likely to be shallow and quickly tested.
